reading_rule: Complete selected scientific source values, with custody-only fields removed as documented. Author-state tokens remain dated source history; original later qualification governs scientific acceptance.

source_record.authority: Author synthesis of actual recorded primary-source readings. Dates identify works or explicitly attributed accounts; no exclusive invention claim. A recipient's testimony can establish its stated use without establishing the full content or priority of an uninspected predecessor.
source_record.source_resolution: Every source_id resolves to SOURCE_TABLE.json and SOURCE_REFERENCE.md. Actual versions, URLs, observation pointers and read scopes are authoritative there. Exact recipient passages below identify the evidence for each edge. No sibling Evolved study is used.

timeline.development: Host/IMP communication conventions and acknowledged delivery context; not a claimed direct origin of all end-to-end reasoning.
Actor, synchronous-process and event-order formalisms supply different abstractions. Logical and physical clock reasoning coexist in the 1978 ordering paper.
Database logging, atomic commitment and replicated voting develop with explicit underlying recovery and failure assumptions.
Arbitrary-fault agreement, asynchronous impossibility, partial synchrony, global-state snapshots and view-based replication address different contracts.
Endpoint responsibility, RPC semantics, epidemic repair, semantic compensation and bounded-clock cache leases expose distinct completion and recovery boundaries.
Object-history correctness, causal/atomic multicast, sessions, isolation criticism and failure detectors refine guarantees and their costs.
Paxos exposition, practical Byzantine state-machine replication and formal CAP analysis preserve different assumptions; none is a single replacement for the others.
Coordination services, weakly consistent storage, CRDTs, causal systems, bounded-clock transactions and coordination-avoidance taxonomies combine older mechanisms under new workloads.
Streaming, checkpointing, phase-specific quorum reasoning, transactional messaging and workflow semantics articulate increasingly explicit interfaces; formal and practitioner work interact.

Incident analysis, selective tracing, storage fault tools, integrity detection, agent translation and edge orchestration extend empirical questions. Publication date, accessed version and evaluation population remain separate.

edges.passage: S101 complete RFC body; S043 pp8–9 history and references, with RFNM discussion referring to BBN1822 December1981.
edges.claim: Both discuss communication responsibilities, but the inspected end-to-end history does not establish transmission from RFC1.
edges.limit: Functional similarity and an early date are not direct descent. Other named antecedents in S043 remain attributed to that recipient account.

edges.passage: S002 conclusions/acknowledgments and §7.7–7.9; its Atkinson/Hewitt1976 reference is not the S0011973 paper.
edges.claim: The two formalisms share a communication subject but differ in rendezvous, buffering and response assumptions.
edges.limit: A related author reference does not identify direct use of this exact earlier paper. Dijkstra/IFIP WG2.3 inspiration is explicitly acknowledged by S002.

edges.passage: S011 §4.1 Implementing a state machine; S003 Ordering Events Totally pp560–562.
edges.claim: The recipient explicitly attributes the state-machine idea used in its exposition to Lamport1978.
edges.limit: This is an acknowledged input, not exclusive priority or proof that every replicated-state-machine design descends through this path.

edges.passage: S011 §4.2 editorial note; S010 view/history and view-change sections.
edges.claim: The recipient acknowledges apparently equivalent view-management ideas in VR.
edges.limit: Acknowledged similarity does not establish that Paxos was copied from VR or that their complete protocols and failure models are identical.

edges.passage: S012 abstract/introduction and design discussion; inspected membership, client and evaluation sections.
edges.claim: Raft explicitly motivates a different decomposition and understandability approach in relation to Paxos.
edges.limit: The source's student experiment and algorithm exposition are different evidence classes. Similarity to VR is also acknowledged; no exclusive ancestry.

edges.passage: N002 §5 weakens Paxos proof assumptions; §7 reconfiguration discussion; S011 ballot safety fragments.
edges.claim: Flexible Paxos identifies cross-phase intersection as the relevant requirement, permitting different quorum choices.
edges.limit: The inspected recipient does not establish a general dynamic-membership implementation; a proposal to use Vertical Paxos principles is not an inspection of S014.

edges.passage: S013 PDFp7 and pp12–13 explicitly attribute vector-time foundations to Fidge and Mattern and causal-delivery development to Schiper.
edges.claim: Recipient testimony establishes an attributed input to its causal multicast construction.
edges.limit: S032's body and the other original predecessor bodies were not inspected here. This edge does not prove exclusive invention, full theorem content or priority.

edges.passage: S018 introduction and termination discussion pp140–142; S017 §§5.8.3.2–5.8.3.3.
edges.claim: The recipient cites database transaction work and modifies an SDD-1 backup-selection mechanism while studying nonblocking commitment.
edges.limit: The SDD-1 body was not separately inspected. Nonblocking claims retain S018's communication/failure premises and are not a universal replacement verdict.

edges.passage: S055 §4.3 cites Garcia-Molina/Salem; §§7.1–7.4 implementation and §9.1 limits; S019 §§1,5–7,9.
edges.claim: The data-oriented workflow discussion explicitly uses saga/compensation ideas in a different transactional system context.
edges.limit: Concurrent backout is not an implemented general guarantee in the inspected prototype. Its related R3 references are not independent studies.

edges.passage: S097 §§2.1,3 and acknowledgment; S019 semantic compensation and application-design discussion.
edges.claim: SagaLLM explicitly adapts saga concepts to agent planning and attributes inspiration.
edges.limit: This documents transmission of a design idea, not transfer of a database proof, independence of validators or guaranteed external compensation.

edges.claim: The recipient relates its session/cache-token design to lease overhead and explicitly acknowledges other cache predecessors.
edges.limit: Chubby also credits AFS and Echo; it is not simply a relabeled copy of one lease algorithm. Its 2006 deployment account is not a current implementation audit.

edges.passage: S033 §1 and Theorems1–4; S036 §3 and §4.1.2.
edges.claim: HLC situates logical/physical clock combination relative to TrueTime and vector/logical clocks.
edges.limit: HLC timestamps and Spanner's uncertainty/commit-wait protocol are different mechanisms. The recipient's rhetoric does not erase earlier physical-clock theory.

edges.passage: S030 inspected portfolio/related-work passages on shopping-cart anomaly; S037 §4.4.
edges.claim: CRDT discussion uses reconciliation anomalies such as shopping-cart resurrection to motivate more explicit replicated-data semantics.
edges.limit: A useful corrected example does not make every Dynamo application wrong or every application invariant convergent.

edges.passage: N003 §6 and its explicit RR7506 portfolio/RR7686 proof references.
edges.claim: The short paper and longer reports belong to the same author-team CRDT development and provide complementary exposition.
edges.limit: They are distinct bibliographic works/versions but not independent replications; the referenced proof supplement was not inspected.

edges.passage: N004 §§1–4.2; S025 definitions and impossibility/alternative sections.
edges.claim: Gilbert and Lynch revisit their formalization and its practical interpretation.
edges.limit: N004 is not Brewer's S026, and does not upgrade that body's reading status. Repeated exposition by the same authors is not independent proof replication.

edges.passage: S039 §5 taxonomy explicitly builds on Adya and partly ANSI SQL/Berenson; S022 §§1–2.2 and §5.
edges.claim: HAT organizes availability and isolation questions using prior transactional anomaly definitions.
edges.limit: Only the inspected Berenson branch is directly available here; the uninspected Adya body is recipient-attributed. This is not a universal equivalence of isolation names.

edges.passage: S038 §7 names HAT/RAMP and distinguishes CALM, CRDT and commutativity; §§3–4 define invariant confluence.
edges.claim: The recipient develops invariant-centered coordination reasoning alongside its author team's prior availability work.
edges.limit: Shared authors and conceptual development are not independent replication. The original author later inspected arXiv1402.2237v4 Appendix B lines482–514 and model/theorem/discussion excerpts184–231, as preserved in the inherited observation and reading event. Other appendices, whole-paper reading, complete published/extended-version correspondence, mechanization and deployment validation are not established. r2 reconciles this existing scoped reading; it performs no new primary reading.

edges.passage: S048 §2 explicitly extends Chandy–Lamport; §§4.2–4.3 state channel and cycle handling; S004 §§2–4.
edges.claim: Barrier snapshotting adapts consistent-state capture to distributed dataflow and its graph structure.
edges.limit: The adaptation's channel/blocking and recovery premises remain necessary; its benchmark does not establish every checkpoint backend's performance.

edges.passage: S047 p1792 footnote identifies FlumeJava/MillWheel technology; §2 describes SDK evolution from FlumeJava.
edges.claim: The recipient supplies direct testimony about implementation and conceptual inputs to the Dataflow model.
edges.limit: This does not substitute for reading MillWheel or FlumeJava themselves, and does not establish that every stream processor has this ancestry.

edges.passage: S091 §2.2 invokes end-to-end reasoning for integrity and §5 compares fault-study approaches; S043 pp5–9.
edges.claim: The recipient uses endpoint integrity reasoning to motivate storage-fault scrutiny beyond replication count.
edges.limit: Its selected fault experiment is evidence for its systems and faults, not independent validation of every end-to-end argument or common-mode scenario.

edges.passage: S052 introduction documents work with the DF team and influence on two backend designs; §§5–6 supply formal scope.
edges.claim: The source describes formalization informed by a practical system and subsequent design feedback.
edges.limit: The backend implementations were not independently audited. A collaboration report is not an operational outcome study.
